questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total frequency N = 5 + 7 + 4 + 8 + 2 = 26.

Median class is determined by the cumulative frequency just greater than or equal to N ÷ 2.

N ÷ 2 = 26 ÷ 2 = 13.

Cumulative frequencies (CF): 5 → 12 → 16.

The 13th term falls in the group with CF 16, which corresponds to x = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

f (frequency): 5, 7, 4, 8, 2

**Formula Used:**

If the total number of observations (N) is even, Median = [ (N ÷ 2)th term + (N ÷ 2 + 1)th term ] ÷ 2.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us calculate the Cumulative Frequency (CF) for each class:

⇒ For x = 1, f = 5 → CF = 5

⇒ For x = 2, f = 7 → CF = 5 + 7 = 12

⇒ For x = 3, f = 4 → CF = 12 + 4 = 16

⇒ For x = 4, f = 8 → CF = 16 + 8 = 24

⇒ For x = 5, f = 2 → CF = 24 + 2 = 26

⇒ Total frequency N = 26, which is an even number.

⇒ Position 1 = N ÷ 2 = 13th observation.

⇒ Position 2 = (N ÷ 2) + 1 = 14th observation.

⇒ The CF just greater than 12 is 16, meaning both the 13th and 14th observations fall under x = 3.

⇒ Median = (3 + 3) ÷ 2 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean

Mean is the arithmetic average of a distribution, calculated as Mean = ∑(f × x) ÷ ∑f.

Mode

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. In this distribution, x = 4 has the highest frequency (8), so the Mode is 4.

Empirical Relationship

For moderately skewed distributions, the empirical relationship between mean, median, and mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: Determine the positive value of 'k' for which the equations x² + kx + 64 = 0 and x² - 8x + k = 0 will both have real roots.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Equations: x² + kx + 64 = 0 and x² - 8x + k = 0

**Formula used:**

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 to have real roots, the discriminant must be non-negative:

Discriminant (Δ) = b² - 4ac ≥ 0

**Calculations:**

For the first equation x² + kx + 64 = 0:

Δ₁ = k² - 4 × 1 × 64

⇒ k² - 256 ≥ 0

⇒ k² ≥ 256

⇒ |k| ≥ 16

For the second equation x² - 8x + k = 0:

Δ₂ = (-8)² - 4 × 1 × k

⇒ 64 - 4k ≥ 0

⇒ 64 ≥ 4k

⇒ k ≤ 16

Combining the two conditions:

|k| ≥ 16 and k ≤ 16

Thus, k = 16

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The position of the image produced by a concave mirror when an object is placed at a distance such that light rays from the object are parallel to the principal axis is:

options.text: at a point between the principal focus and pole
at the position of the object itself
at a point between the principal focus and the centre of curvature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The principal focus**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When light rays from an object are parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror, they converge after reflection and meet at the **principal focus**.
 
• This is a fundamental property of concave mirrors:
 
• **Parallel rays** to the principal axis always converge at the **focus** after reflection.
 
• Thus, the image will be formed at the principal focus, and it will be **real, inverted**, and highly diminished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae288c9dcb7001f9330e6c4830e1fdce6de95827bc06b2d6f615097a2a2bae90.png]

__
 
• Spherical mirrors are of two types -

 
 
• Convex mirror, and
 
• Concave mirror.
 
 
 
• The image formed by the spherical mirrors depends on the position of the object.

 
• Convex mirror: If the outer surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface then it is called a convex mirror. It is also called the diverging mirror.

 
 
• The nature of the image formed by a convex mirror does not depend on the distance of the object from the mirror. These images are always virtual, smaller than the object, and situated behind the mirror.
 
 
 
• Concave mirror: If the inner surface of the spherical mirror is the reflecting surface, then it is called a concave mirror. It is also called a focusing mirror/converging mirror.
 
 
• The size of the image produced by these mirrors can be larger or smaller than the object, depending upon the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
• The concave mirror can form both real as well as virtual images of any object.
 
 
 
• Plane mirrors are the most commonly used mirrors. Lateral inversion is seen in the plane mirror.

questions.question: Consider that a mature blue whale is 30.0 m long. On the other hand a baby whale is 10.0 m long. Where should the baby whale be placed in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15.0 m so that one can observe a real image of the baby whale as that of the size of a mature whale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2__**0 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Step 1: Calculate the Required Magnification**

Given

__
 
• Length of mature whale h_i= -30m
 
• Length of baby whale h_o= 10m

The magnification required is: m= (h_i)/(h_o)= (-30)/(10)=-3

This means the image needs to be three times the size of the object.

**Step 2: Apply Magnification Formula for Mirrors**

The magnification (m) is also related to the object distance (p) and the image distance (q) by: m=-(q)/(p)

We know m = -3, So (q)/(p)= -3

q=-3p

**Step 3: Use the Mirror Formula**

The mirror formula is: (1)/(f)= (1)/(p)+(1)/(q), where f is the focal length of the mirror.

Given the focal length of the mirror f=-15m, substitute q=-3p into the mirror formula:

(1)/(-15)=(1)/(-p)+ (1)/(-3p)

-(1)/(15)=( -3-1)/(3p)

(1)/(15)=(4)/(3p)

p=20

 

The baby whale should be placed **20.0 m in front of the concave mirror** to produce a **real image three times the size of the baby whale**, making it appear as long as a mature whale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with its reflecting surface curved inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It can form real and virtual images depending on the position of the object relative to the focal point and center of curvature.
 
• When an object is placed beyond the center of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and diminished.
 
• When an object is placed between the focal point and the center of curvature, the image formed is real, inverted, and magnified.

__
 
• A 12 V battery is connected across a 250 Ω resistance.
 
• We need to **calculate the heat produced in 5 second**s.
 
• **Given:**
 
 
• **Voltage (V) = 12 V**
 
• **Resistance (R) = 250 Ω**
 
• **Time (t) = 5 s**
 
 
 
• **Calculation:**
 
 
• ** T**he heat produced (H) can be calculated using **Joule's law of heating, which is:**
 
 
• **H = (V² / R) * t**
 
• H = (12² / 250) * 5
 
• H = (144 / 250) * 5
 
• H = 0.576 * 5
 
• H = 2.88 J
 
 
 
• Therefore, **the heat produced in 5 seconds is 2.88 Joules.**

• The Joule's law of heating states that heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current flowing through a resistor, **directly proportional to the resistance **of the given resistor and directly proportional to the time for which the currents flows through the resistor.
 
 
• Therefore H=I2Rt, where H is Heat, I is current, R is Resistance, t is time.

questions.question: Simplify (7x - 1)³ + (7x + 1)³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct algebraic identity: (a − b)³ + (a + b)³ = 2a³ + 6ab².

Here, substitute a = 7x and b = 1.

⇒ 2(7x)³ + 6(7x)(1)²

⇒ 2(343x³) + 42x

⇒ 686x³ + 42x

**∴ The correct answer is 686x³ + 42x.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The expression is (7x − 1)³ + (7x + 1)³.

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab²

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3a²b + 3ab²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us expand both terms individually using the formulas.

⇒ (7x − 1)³ = (7x)³ − 1³ − 3(7x)²(1) + 3(7x)(1)²

⇒ (7x − 1)³ = 343x³ − 1 − 147x² + 21x

⇒ (7x + 1)³ = (7x)³ + 1³ + 3(7x)²(1) + 3(7x)(1)²

⇒ (7x + 1)³ = 343x³ + 1 + 147x² + 21x

⇒ Now, add the two expanded forms together:

⇒ (343x³ − 1 − 147x² + 21x) + (343x³ + 1 + 147x² + 21x)

⇒ The terms with opposite signs cancel out (−1 and +1, −147x² and +147x²).

⇒ = (343x³ + 343x³) + (21x + 21x)

⇒ = 686x³ + 42x

**∴ The correct answer is 686x³ + 42x.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference of Cubes

Basic algebraic identities are: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Algebraic Identities for Squares

Similarly, for squares: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Cubes Subtraction Trick

Similar to the sum of cubes, the difference expression can be simplified directly as: (a + b)³ − (a − b)³ = 2b³ + 6a²b.

__
 
• **Newland assumed that only 56 elements exist in nature**__.

 __
 
• **In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then-known elements in order of increasing atomic mass.**
 
• He started with the element with the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended with Thorium which was the 56th element.
 
• He f**ound that every eighth element has the same properties as the first.**
 
• He compared it to the octave found in music.
 
• That's why he called it the 'law of octaves'.
 
• This is known as '**Newlands' Law of Octaves**'.
 
• The properties of lithium and sodium were found to be similar in Newlands' octave.

• **Law of Octaves** was applicable only up to calcium, as after calcium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.

 
 
• It was assumed by Newlands that **only 56 elements** existed in nature and no more elements would be discovered in the future.
 
• But, later on, several new elements were discovered, whose properties did not fit into the Law of Octaves. 
 
 
 
• In 1869, just five years after John Newlands put forward his Law of Octaves, a Russian chemist called Dmitri Mendeleev published a periodic table.

• Copper atoms bond together with metallic bonds, allowing electrons to move freely, giving copper its excellent electrical conductivity.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding:**
 
 
• **Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative element like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine,** and is attracted to a lone pair of electrons on another electronegative atom.
 
• **Example: Water (H₂O)**
 
• In water, hydrogen bonds form between the hydrogen atoms of one molecule and the oxygen atom of another, giving water its high boiling point and surface tension.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Bonding:**
 
 
• Ionic bonding** occurs when one atom donates an electron to another, creating positively and negatively charged ions that are attracted to each other.**
 
• **Example: Sodium chloride (NaCl)**
 
• Sodium (Na) donates an electron to chlorine (Cl), forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that are held together by electrostatic forces.

__
 
• A **decrease in revenue receipts** increases the gross fiscal deficit.
 
• **Gross fiscal deficit:-**
 
 
• **It is the excess of total expenditure, including loans net of recovery over net of revenue and non-debt capital receipts. **
 
• It is an indicator of the total borrowings needed by the government.
 
• GFD is calculated as follows: **GFD = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)**

• **Gross Primary Deficit**:

 
 
• This refers to the difference between the **gross fiscal deficit** (the total borrowing requirements of the government) and the **net interest liabilities** (the interest payments made by the government on its outstanding debt).
 
• Essentially, it reflects the government's borrowing needs excluding the interest on debt.
 
• Gross Primary Deficit = **Gross Fiscal Deficit** – **Net Interest Liabilities**
 
 
 
• **Net Interest Liabilities**:
 
 
• This is the difference between the government's **interest payments** on its borrowings and the **interest receipts** (the income the government earns from its own investments or loans).
 
• If the government earns more from interest than it pays, the net interest liability would be negative.
 
• Net Interest Liabilities = **Interest Payments** – **Interest Receipts**
 
 
 
• **These concepts are used to assess the fiscal health of a government by separating the effects of past borrowing (interest payments) from the current fiscal position (primary deficit).**

__
 
• **India became a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO)** on 1 January 1995.
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) is **an intergovernmental organization that regulates international trade.**
 
• **WTO officially commenced on 1 January 1995** under the Marrakesh Agreement, **replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**.
 
• As a member of the WTO, India has to adhere to its rules and regulations and can benefit from the international trading system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO)**

 
 
• The** WTO is the only global international organization dealing with the rules of trade between nations**.
 
• Its **main function is to ensure that trade flows as smoothly**, predictably, and freely as possible.
 
• The WTO provides a forum for negotiating agreements aimed at reducing obstacles to international trade and ensuring a level playing field for all, thus contributing to economic growth and development.
 
• The **WTO also provides a legal and institutional framework for the implementation and monitoring of these agreements,** as well as for settling disputes arising from their interpretation and application.
 
 
 
• **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)**
 
 
• The **GATT was a legal agreement between many countries**, whose overall purpose was to promote international trade by reducing or eliminating trade barriers such as tariffs or quotas.
 
• It **was signed by 23 nations in Geneva on October 30, 1947, and took effect on January 1, 1948.**
 
• The GATT was intended to boost economic recovery after World War II through reconstructing and liberalizing global trade.
 
• The GATT continued to exist until it was replaced by the WTO on January 1, 1995.
 
 
 
• **Marrakesh Agreement**
 
 
• The **Marrakesh Agreement established the World Trade Organization, signed in Marrakesh, Morocco, on April 15, 1994.**
 
• The agreement marked the culmination of the Uruguay Round of GATT negotiations, which lasted from 1986 to 1994.
 
• It resulted in the most significant reform of the global trading system since the GATT was created in 1948.
 
• The Marrakesh Agreement incorporated the GATT framework and expanded it to include new areas such as services and intellectual property.

questions.question: A certain sum invested at 12% simple interest per annum after 5 years yields an interest of ₹19,200. What is the sum invested?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹19,200

Rate (r) = 12% per annum

Time (t) = 5 years

**Formula used:**

SI = (P times r times t)/(100) 

Where, P = Principal

**Calculation:**

19,200 = (P times 12 times 5)/(100) 

⇒ 19,200 = (60P)/(100) 

⇒ 19,200 = 0.6P

⇒ P = (19,200)/(0.6) 

⇒ P = ₹32,000

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Suppose a lamp of 25 Ω is connected across a battery. The heat produced by the lamp per second is 100 J. The potential difference across the lamp is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 50 V**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **heat produced per second is the power (P) of the lamp. **
 
• In this case, P = 100 J/s = 100 W.
 
• The **power of a resistor (or lamp) is related to the voltage (V)** across it and its **resistance (R) by the formula**:
 
 
• P = V² / R
 
 
 
• **Rearrange the power formula to isolate V:** V = sqrt(P * R)
 
• **Substitute the given values**:
 
 
• V = sqrt(100 W * 25 Ω)
 
• V = sqrt(2500) V = 50 volts
 
 
 
• 
 
**Therefore, the potential difference across the lamp is 50 volts.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
**Joule's law of heating​:**

 
 
• According to the Joule's law of heating, heat produced when a current 'I' flows through a material of resistance 'R' for a period of time 'T' is I2RT.
 
• The Joule's law of heating states that heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of the current flowing through a resistor, directly proportional to the resistance of the given resistor and directly proportional to the time for which the currents flows through the resistor.
 
• Therefore H = I2Rt, where H is Heat, I is current, R is Resistance, t is time.
